claim_reviews.rationale: Kingery table 1 sample 86-1 and footnote document collection source and bench-like feature; Dubreuil p.124 calls the match to Perrot’s Shelter 1 description probable rather than a confirmed specimen match. Source record or field catalogue/dispatch comparison remains the correct next route. A newly sampled fragment would not be 86-1.

Haklay and Gopher Early Natufian remains and fig.1 identify layer II and Shelter 1; archive JP557 finding aid pp.21–22 labels La grande tombe (abri 1), plate 25 locus 1, while other plates include locus 3. Independently viewed the reproduced field photograph with later Shelter 1/3 labels. Published photo does not itself carry the laboratory specimen identifier.

Dubreuil p.124 §1.4.1.4 reproduces Perrot 1966 p.445 on feature dimensions and polished coating; quotation remains a secondary reproduction since original 1966 paper not opened. Perrot 1975 original pp.485–486 and plate I concern House 131; archive JP664/JP665 lists preparatory records. The earlier and later original reports were not conflated.

Kingery et al. 1988 pp.224–226, table 1 and footnote explicitly identify 86-1, site, material, interpretation and collection credit; do not identify field position or catalogue accession. HUJI collection page and Smithsonian/Harvard finding aids are leads rather than custody or absence proof.

MSH Mondes Perrot fonds finding aid pp.8, 11, 14, 21–22 identifies JP216 notebooks, JP220 sample catalogue, JP553 sections and JP557 plate 25 locus 1. These describe potential documents, not an observed sample link. JP646 photo series identifiers provide route, not particular figure attribution.

Dubreuil p.124 uses probablement; Valla et al. 2007 pp.146–148, 162–165/table 5 reports distinct Locus 239 material and sample identifiers; Es Sebar et al. 2022 distinguishes several carbonate categories. None independently identifies or retests 86-1.
Shelter 1 field evidence and modern disturbance provide context but cannot establish function of sample 86-1; decision properly separates context, identity and use.

No discovery file or established link added; baseline candidate companion_of remains a question. Site coincidence and a probable descriptive comparison do not satisfy the exact companion_of functional relationship or establish a dated specimen event.
